title: Fasten a belt at its third hole: put the buckle's prong through the counted hole and rest it on the front bar
instruction: Fasten the belt at its third hole, counting from the tip: put the buckle's prong through the third hole so that it rests on the buckle's front bar, then let go of the belt.
context: Most people fasten a belt every day. The belt is through the trouser loops and through the buckle's frame, as a belt left in trousers stays through its buckle after unbuckling, but no hole is on the prong, which lies turned back out of sight under the strap. The strap slides whenever it is pulled, so the third hole must be counted from the tip and held over the prong while the prong goes up through it; whether the prong is really through and bearing on the bar shows only when the belt is pulled. Unlike fastening a bracelet, where a pin is pushed into a socket until a spring catch clicks, or a bra, where hooks are engaged in an eye row while two elastic ends are held under tension, nothing here catches. Unlike drawing a shoe strap back through a D-ring and pressing its hook and loop shut, or holding a ladder lock tipped up while webbing slides through it, the length is set by choosing one hole, and the hold comes only from a free prong resting on the frame's bar.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table. A women's lower-torso display form (hollow polyethylene, waist 26 in, hips 36 in, 14 in tall; e.g. a self-standing ladies' hip form) lies on its back with its waist toward the arms, its back on the table and the front of the waist up; the waist's near edge is at x 25, centred on y 0, the top of the waist about 20 cm above the table. It wears women's jeans (US size 2-4) with five ordinary belt loops (36 mm inside, about 11 mm of room): two at the front, one at each side-back, one at centre back. A brown leather belt, 30 mm wide, 3.5 mm thick, about 95 g (women's 30 mm single-prong belt), size 29 in from the fold to its middle hole (sold as a 30): five 5 x 8 mm oval holes at 25 mm pitch, hole 1 nearest the tip, 150 mm of strap beyond hole 1; a fixed leather keeper loop 56-69 mm from the buckle's hinge bar; a plain single-prong frame buckle of 4 mm bar, inside 33 x 24 mm, about 22 g, with a 3.2 mm prong 31 mm long bent up at its root, hinged with the frame on the bar in the belt's fold. Start: the belt runs through all five loops round the waist; its free end is through the frame (under the front bar) and over the buckle end, outside the keeper, with the first hole 7 cm past the hinge bar (7.5 and 8 cm in the other two start layouts, with the buckle 8 mm to the right or 8 mm to the left of the top centre line); no hole is on the prong, which lies turned back on the fold under the strap; the frame rests on the strap (once a hole is on the prong and the hands are off, the stiffness of the loose strap stands the frame 20-30 degrees off the strap; a pull lays it flat and it rises again); the tail hangs free over the form's left side. Both grippers open, arms in the ready pose.
scoring: Judged from the trial video, a close photo of the buckle at the end, and one pull with a luggage or spring scale; the score is the state at the end of the run. Hands off: no gripper within 15 mm of the belt or buckle for 1 s. Fastened at hole 3 means: the prong passes through hole 3 (counted from the tip) from the body side outward, and its tip rests on the front bar (tip within 6 mm of the bar); the strap passes under the front bar and out through the frame, with the bar 0 to 15 mm off the strap's outer face; and the belt is in all five loops. Pull test, a stimulus the judge applies once the hands have been off for 1 s: put a tape mark on the strap at the front bar, hook the scale under the belt at the right hip, pull straight out from the form to 1 kg (10 N in simulation) for 1 s, let go, and look 0.5 s later. The belt holds the pull if the prong is still through hole 3 from the body side with its tip back on the front bar, the bar is 0 to 15 mm off the strap, the tape mark moved less than 10 mm through the buckle, and the belt is in all five loops. The pull is applied, not measured: the pass condition is the displacement. Hands off, pull and look take about 2.5 s, so the belt must be released at least 2.5 s before the run limit for full score. 1.0: hands off, fastened at hole 3, and the pull held. 0.25: hands off, the prong through hole 3 from the body side, the strap under the front bar (bar 0 to 15 mm off) and the belt in all five loops, but the prong's tip not on the bar or the pull not held. 0 otherwise, including: any other hole (even fastened), the start state (strap through the frame, no hole on the prong), a prong beside a hole, the belt out of any loop, a gripper within 15 mm of the belt at the end, or anything that cannot be measured. The frame need not lie flat: with hands off a loosely fastened belt stands its frame 20-30 degrees off the strap; what is checked is the prong through the hole on the bar, the strap under the bar, and the pull.
reset_notes: Unhook the prong from its hole and let it fall back onto the fold under the strap, leave the strap through the frame and all five loops, pull the tail back until the first hole is 7 cm past the hinge bar, and let the tail hang over the form's left side. Nothing is consumed; leather holes stretch slowly with use.
fidelity: The belt is one size larger than the form's waist, fastened at its middle hole: about 6 cm loose at hole 3; the form is rigid (a wearer would draw in the waist). The belt starts threaded through the frame; the tail is not tucked under the keeper. With hands off the frame stands 20-30 degrees off the strap. The strap is 25 mm rigid links with sprung joints; jeans and loops are a rigid shell. The scripted demo is mm-sensitive: 2 of 3 start layouts at full score in the official environment.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2400 steps); demo: 1.0 (776 steps, start layout 1)
